messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — proposal to wire GPU ECC/Xid/flaky-card signals into an automated cordon+drain flow that works for both k8s and Slurm. Key goals: safety (no silent evictions), observability (who/why), and an easy dry-run mode.

sanjay: How do we avoid killing long-running training jobs? we have 48h jobs that are fragile to preemption.

alex: plan is: 1) classify signals (transient vs persistent), 2) soft remediation first (nvml reset, rebind drivers), 3) on persistent failures mark node as Unhealthy and taint with `gpu-unhealthy=true:NoSchedule`, 4) notify owners + start graceful drain with long grace period + requeue behavior for Slurm.

maria: can we add a circuit-breaker that prevents auto-drain if the node has >1 very-late job? or at least escalate to pager after N drains in 24h. also :eyes: on audit trail.

alex: yes — propose thresholds: transient = single Xid within 5m; persistent = 3 Xid/ECC faults across any GPU on node within 15m OR continuous ECC bit flips over 10m. persistent -> begin remediation steps and then cordon after remediation fails. circuit-breaker: if node already auto-drained twice in last 24h, open a human ticket instead of auto-evict.

infra-bot: [metric-alert] gpu-exporter.gpu01: ECC errors spike (3/10m) — node nv-host-221 flagged by rule gpu.ecc.persistent

olga: for metrics/integration: we can use node-exporter + custom nvml exporter (gpu-health-exporter). Alertmanager route should add `autodrain` label when alert matches `gpu.ecc.persistent`. That label triggers our choreography service (k8s controller / slurm-svc).

kevin: implementation details for k8s: controller should support dry-run mode that just taints nodes and posts Slack thread + runbook link. When enabled it will run: ```
# cordon + drain with long grace
kubectl cordon nv-host-221
kubectl drain nv-host-221 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=300 --force --timeout=30m
```

kevin: for Slurm we don't delete jobs — we set node state to DRAIN with reason and optionally requeue dependent jobs. example: ```
scontrol update NodeName=nv-host-221 State=DRAIN Reason="ECC persistent, auto-drain"
scontrol show node nv-host-221
```

sanjay: what about GPUs that support gpu reset? can we try `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <id>` before draining?

alex: yes — remediation step order: 1) run gpu-health-check script (dump dmesg + nvidia-smi -q), 2) attempt driver soft-rebind (systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced), 3) attempt gpu reset where supported, 4) if still failing -> taint + start drain. All retries logged to the runbook and incident ticket.

maria: we should also add a per-cluster policy: low-util dev clusters = aggressive auto-drain; prod clusters = conservative + always notify + require human ack for nodes with running jobs >24h.

olga: ops note: ensure the controller honors `pod disruption budgets` for k8s; for bursty batch systems we should allow eviction only if PDBs permit or fall back to cordon-only + operator alert.

kevin: test plan: 1) unit tests for classification logic, 2) e2e in staging with synthetic ECC alerts, 3) 1-week canary in non-critical AZ with dry-run then with real drain and 4) postmortem on every auto-drain to validate thresholds.

alex: warnings: some Xid codes are harmless (class 31 transient), need mapping table in controller. We'll only treat Xid classes mapped to persistent or driver-fatal as candidates for auto-drain.

infra-bot: [workflow] created runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-autodrain — includes slack playbook, slurm commands, and rollback steps.

maria: :thumbsup: also add metric histogram of time-to-recover vs time-to-drain so we can tune threshold to minimize job disruption.

kevin: I'll sketch a prototype controller this week. It will expose flags: `--dry-run`, `--max-auto-drains-per-node=2`, `--grace-period-secs=300`.

alex: sounds good. next steps: kevin + olga pair on controller + alertmanager routing, sanjay + maria define cluster policies, ops-runbook finalization. will post RFC this Friday.

sanjay: agree. can we include a simulated Slurm job generator to validate requeue behavior?

alex: yes — add that to test plan. thanks all. :rocket:
